policy.note: Direct dependencies only. Transitive dependencies inherit approval from their allowlisted direct parent and are deliberately not filed. See README.md for what that does and does not protect against.

npm.identityNote: An npm package's only manifest-visible owner is its scope. Registry `maintainers` is mutable metadata that a consumer never declares, so it is not a checkable identity. Unscoped packages therefore cannot be approved by author and must be listed one at a time.

pypi.identityNote: PyPI has no namespace at all -- a requirement string carries no owner, and project ownership is not derivable from what a consumer declares. Author-level approval is therefore NOT EXPRESSIBLE for Python, and every distribution is listed individually. This is a real difference between registries, not an oversight.

pytest.reason: The Python test runner for the -py mirror packages.

freshness.evidence: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest -- commits on the default branch 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18, pushed 2026-09-20, not archived
freshness.why: Last PyPI release 9.1.1 on 2026-06-19, which crossed the 92-day bar on 2026-09-19. The repository is committed to weekly; the project tags slowly, which is the gap this override exists for.

ruff.reason: Linter and formatter for the Python packages.

mypy.reason: Static type checking for the Python packages.

crates._note: crates.io has no namespace, so author-level approval is not expressible and every crate is listed individually -- the same shape as pypi. A `git` or `path` dependency in a Cargo.toml is not a registry dependency at all; it must be first-party, because nothing about it is checkable here.

packageGrants._note: A grant approves a library FOR ONE PACKAGE, because that package exists to wrap or host it. It does not approve the library anywhere else. Keys are the manifest name (package.json name / composer.json name / [project] name), falling back to the repo directory name for manifests that declare none.

Chosen over echarts on measured evidence: echarts has no update-in-place API for a candlestick series, so a tick costs 18.45ms against 2.36ms on a realistic two-pane trading chart, at 3.6x the bundle. See .ai/plans/fancy-trading.md section 1.
lightweight-charts.review: ATTRIBUTION IS OWED, AND IT IS INHERITED BY OUR CONSUMERS. Apache-2.0 with a NOTICE that npm does NOT ship. Every commercial consumer of a fancy-trading-ui chart built on this must display either the on-chart attributionLogo (which defaults to true -- pass it through, never silently false) or the NOTICE text plus a link to https://www.tradingview.com/ on a user-facing page. The exact bytes to reproduce are in .ai/knowledge/lightweight-charts-attribution.md; copy them, do not retype -- the (c) in the NOTICE is Cyrillic U+0441, so grep '(c)' will not find it. Not legal advice.
